text:
Alex Chen: Ran a probe this morning using the new continuous-batching classifier. I split traffic by prompt-length buckets and decode-rate buckets and collected p50/p95 latencies + kernel choices.

Alex Chen: Buckets used: prompt_len: [0-32,33-128,129-512,513+]; decode_rate: [<50 tok/s, 50-200 tok/s, >200 tok/s]. Classifier maps fast decoders to larger token budgets.

Alex Chen: Quick profiler dump (short):
```
# sample request profile
bucket: 33-128 / 50-200 tok/s
kernel: fused_attn_v2
kv_cache: warm (hit=0.82)
batch_size: 12
decode_tokens: 48
p50_latency_ms: 78
p95_latency_ms: 210
throughput_rps: 14.2
```

Priya Patel: Interesting — fused_attn_v2 shows gains for mid-lengths. Did you see any regression on >512 prompts where kernel falls back to tiled_gemm?

Alex Chen: Yes. For 513+ we saw fallback to tiled_gemm on Ampere due to memory layout; p95 jumped ~40%.

Maria Gomez: KV-cache warm fraction looks low for some buckets. We should track warm/cold transitions: prefix caching misses when requests interleave. This hurts long prompts.

Ryan Li: For queue policy, what token_budget did you use per bucket? Currently we use a flat 256 token budget per batch.

Alex Chen: For the probe I used adaptive targets: [64, 256, 512, 1024] mapped to the prompt buckets. That reduced p50 for 33-128 by ~12% but increased p95 for 513+.

Priya Patel: Can we try token-budget cap + decode_rate constraint? Eg cap budget to max(64, min(1024, floor(decode_rate * 2))) so slow decoders don't form huge batches.

Maria Gomez: Also consider queue-time cutoff at 12ms for fast paths. Fast decoders shouldn't wait long for slow arrivals.

bench-bot: perf summary: AB test candidate A (flat_256) vs B (adaptive_by_bucket)
A: overall p50 95ms / p95 310ms
B: overall p50 86ms / p95 335ms (improved median, worse tail)

Alex Chen: We need to reduce tail without losing median. Proposal: change classifier to be more aggressive on decode-rate separation and enforce kv_cache affinity window (keep requests that hit same cache in same bucket for 50ms).

Priya Patel: Agreed. Also add a kernel-selection override: if model_seq_len > 1024 and batch token sum > 2000 prefer tiled_gemm with prefetch tweak to avoid late fallback.

Ryan Li: I'll schedule a canary run with 10k requests across hours; include 20% traffic in region-us-west2. Want perf-bot to collect per-bucket p50/p95 and boxplots.

perf-bot: Canary scheduled: id=cb-1768754321, start=2026-03-17T15:12:00Z, sample=10k, channels=[eng-runtime], notify=@Alex Chen @Priya Patel @Maria Gomez

Alex Chen: Thanks — tagging @Maria Gomez to add cache affinity metrics and @Priya Patel to tweak classifier thresholds. We'll reconvene after canary results. :thumbsup:
